title: HVAC Zone 3 temperature oscillation causing comfort complaints
description: Zone 3 in Building A is experiencing temperature oscillations of +/- 4°F around setpoint. Occupants reporting discomfort. PID loop tuning suspected. VAV box damper actuator may be hunting.
resolution: Retuned PID parameters: reduced proportional gain from 8 to 4, increased integral time from 2min to 5min. Verified damper actuator stroke and calibrated. Oscillation resolved within 30 minutes.

title: Chiller plant staging failure during peak load
description: Chiller 2 failed to stage on during peak cooling demand. Building load exceeded 85% capacity but only Chiller 1 was running. BACnet communication to Chiller 2 controller showed intermittent timeouts.
resolution: Replaced faulty BACnet MSTP trunk cable between junction box JB-14 and Chiller 2 controller. Cable had water damage from condensation. Verified staging sequence operates correctly with both chillers.

title: Lighting schedule override not releasing on weekends
description: Building B lighting zones remain in occupied mode over weekends despite holiday schedule being configured. Override commands from the front-end appear to be sticky. Tenants reported lights on 24/7.
resolution: Found that manual override priority (level 8) was higher than scheduled commands (level 14). Adjusted BACnet priority array to ensure schedule writes at priority 7. Cleared all active overrides and tested across a full weekend cycle.

title: AHU-2 supply fan VFD fault alarm recurring
description: AHU-2 supply fan variable frequency drive is generating fault F51 (overcurrent) every 3-4 hours. Drive auto-resets but causes brief temperature spikes downstream. Motor current draw is near rated FLA.
resolution: Inspected fan belt tension — found belt slipping causing motor to draw excess current during acceleration. Replaced worn belts and adjusted tension. Cleaned VFD heat sink fins which were clogged with dust. No further faults after 72-hour monitoring period.

title: Boiler lead-lag rotation not functioning
description: Boiler system configured for weekly lead-lag rotation but Boiler 1 has been lead for the past 6 weeks. Uneven runtime hours causing accelerated wear on Boiler 1. Boiler 2 shows 40% fewer operating hours.
resolution: Timer function block in PLC program had a rollover bug at the 32-bit integer max for millisecond counter. Reset the timer and changed logic to use date-based rotation instead of elapsed time. Both boilers now alternate weekly as intended.

title: Economizer damper stuck at 100% outdoor air
description: AHU-5 economizer outdoor air damper is fully open regardless of outdoor temperature. Mixed air temperature is too low during cold mornings. Enthalpy sensor reading appears frozen at 28 BTU/lb.
resolution: Replaced failed outdoor air enthalpy sensor (RH element had drifted to 100%). Calibrated new sensor against portable reference. Verified economizer changeover logic resumes normal operation with correct OA enthalpy readings.

title: Fire alarm integration causing false HVAC shutdowns
description: HVAC system performing emergency smoke purge sequence without active fire alarm. Happens 2-3 times per week, usually early morning. No corresponding fire panel events logged during these incidents.
resolution: Traced issue to a noisy dry contact relay between fire panel and BEMS. Contact was bouncing due to loose terminal connection. Re-terminated wiring and added a 2-second debounce filter in the BEMS input module. No false shutdowns in 2 weeks of monitoring.

title: Energy meter data gaps in dashboard reporting
description: Power metering data for floors 5-8 showing gaps of 15-30 minutes throughout the day. Dashboard energy reports are underreporting consumption by approximately 12%. Modbus TCP polling from BEMS to meters times out sporadically.
resolution: Network switch on floor 5 IDF had autonegotiation issues causing packet loss. Forced port speed to 100Mbps full duplex matching meter NIC capabilities. Increased Modbus poll timeout from 3s to 8s as interim measure. Data gaps eliminated after switch configuration change.

title: Cooling tower fan cycling too frequently
description: Cooling tower fans cycling on/off every 2-3 minutes. Condenser water temperature unstable. Fan motors at risk of premature failure from excessive starts. Current differential setpoint is only 1°F.
resolution: Widened condenser water temperature differential from 1°F to 3°F (on at 85°F, off at 82°F). Added minimum run time of 10 minutes to prevent short cycling. Fan starts reduced from 40+/day to under 10/day. Motor current profiles now stable.

title: DDC controller firmware crash after daylight saving time change
description: Three DDC controllers on the 2nd floor rebooted and lost all runtime values during the November DST fallback. Schedules reverted to defaults and occupied/unoccupied transitions were off by one hour for the entire week.
resolution: Applied firmware patch v4.2.1 from manufacturer which fixes the DST date calculation overflow. Restored controller databases from backup. Set NTP synchronization to update time daily instead of relying solely on internal RTC. Verified correct DST handling in test environment.

title: Request to add CO2-based demand ventilation to conference rooms
description: Facilities requesting CO2 demand-controlled ventilation for 12 large conference rooms in Building C. Current system runs at fixed minimum OA regardless of occupancy, wasting energy during unoccupied periods.
resolution: Installed Senva CO2 sensors in each conference room. Programmed DDC controllers to modulate OA damper between 15% (baseline) and 100% based on CO2 levels (800-1200ppm range). Verified airflow meets ASHRAE 62.1 requirements at all setpoints. Estimated 18% reduction in OA heating/cooling energy.

title: Integrate new solar PV monitoring into BEMS dashboard
description: New 500kW rooftop solar array installed on Building A. Need to integrate SolarEdge inverter data into existing BEMS energy dashboard. Data available via Modbus TCP and REST API. Customer wants real-time generation, daily yield, and grid offset metrics.
resolution: Configured Modbus TCP polling from BEMS to SolarEdge gateway at 30-second intervals. Mapped key registers: AC power, daily energy, lifetime energy, inverter status. Created dashboard widgets for real-time generation (kW), daily yield (kWh), monthly trends, and grid offset percentage. Set up alerts for inverter faults and generation anomalies.

title: Discussion on AHU freezestat trips during polar vortex
description: Team discussion about multiple AHU freezestat trips during extreme cold event (-15°F). AHU-1, AHU-3, and AHU-7 all tripped within 2 hours. Preheat coils were active but insufficient. Mixing box temperatures dropped below 35°F triggering safety shutdown.
resolution: Implemented cold weather protocol: added low-limit OA damper position (max 25% below 0°F OA temp), increased preheat coil valve authority, added 15-minute warm-up cycle before economizer enables after freezestat reset. Verified glycol concentration in preheat loops is adequate for -20°F. Created alarm escalation rule for OA temps below -10°F.

title: Troubleshooting BACnet router isolation causing floor 10 offline
description: Floor 10 BEMS points all showing offline. BACnet router BBMD table not propagating to remote subnet. Other floors unaffected. Issue started after network team performed VLAN changes last night.
resolution: Network team had moved BACnet VLAN to a new subnet without updating the BBMD foreign device table entries. Updated BBMD registrations on the floor 10 router and the head-end BACnet/IP router. Verified all 156 points on floor 10 came back online. Added BACnet VLANs to the change management notification list to prevent recurrence.

title: High humidity complaints in server room despite CRAC units running
description: Server room humidity spiking to 75% RH despite both CRAC units showing active dehumidification. IT team concerned about condensation on equipment. BEMS shows both units in cooling mode but humidity not being controlled.
resolution: Found that humidifier on AHU-4 (serving adjacent office space) was over-humidifying and moist air was migrating through unsealed cable penetrations into the server room. Sealed penetrations with fire-stop material. Adjusted AHU-4 humidifier setpoint from 50% to 45% RH. Server room humidity stabilized at 48% RH within 4 hours.

title: Elevator machine room overheating alarm
description: Elevator machine room temperature exceeding 95°F during afternoon hours. Dedicated split AC unit showing clean filter and normal operation on BEMS. Room has two elevator machines generating significant heat. Exhaust fan running but inadequate.
resolution: Split AC unit refrigerant charge was low — found small leak at flare fitting. Recharged with R-410A after repair. Added supplemental exhaust fan with thermostat control (on at 85°F, off at 78°F). Room temperature now maintains below 82°F during peak load.

title: Tenant requesting after-hours HVAC scheduling via web portal
description: Major tenant in Building B wants self-service web portal for requesting after-hours HVAC. Currently requires email to facilities team with 24-hour lead time. Tenant wants same-day, on-demand capability with approval workflow.
resolution: Deployed tenant web portal with BEMS integration. Portal authenticates via SSO and allows tenants to request HVAC for specific zones/floors with 2-hour minimum advance notice. Requests auto-approved for standard zones; restricted zones require facilities manager approval. BEMS receives API call to create temporary schedule override. Billing automatically calculated based on zone size and duration.

title: Water leak detection sensor false alarms in mechanical room
description: Water leak detection rope sensor in mechanical room MR-3 triggering alarms 3-4 times daily. Maintenance has verified no actual leaks. Sensor cable runs near steam piping. Alarms generate after-hours call-outs.
resolution: Condensation from uninsulated steam pipe fittings was dripping onto the leak detection cable. Insulated the exposed fittings with fiberglass pipe wrap. Relocated a 3-foot section of detection cable away from the steam header. Added a 60-second alarm delay to filter momentary moisture events. No false alarms in 10 days of monitoring.

title: Variable refrigerant flow system error code E-23 on outdoor unit
description: VRF outdoor unit #2 displaying error E-23 (high pressure fault) and locking out during afternoon peak. System serves 15 indoor units on the 4th floor. Other outdoor units operating normally.
resolution: Condenser coil was severely fouled with cottonwood debris and dust. High-pressure switch tripping at 410 psig due to poor heat rejection. Chemically cleaned condenser coil and straightened bent fins. Verified subcooling and superheat values returned to normal range. Added quarterly coil cleaning to preventive maintenance schedule.

title: Planning optimal start algorithm tuning for winter
description: Team discussion on optimal start algorithm not bringing building to setpoint before occupancy during winter. Current algorithm underestimates warm-up time when OAT is below 20°F. Building takes 45 minutes longer than predicted to reach 72°F.
resolution: Adjusted optimal start thermal model coefficients: increased building thermal mass factor from 0.6 to 0.85, added wind chill compensation factor, extended maximum pre-start time from 3 hours to 4.5 hours. Incorporated weather forecast API data for next-day OAT prediction instead of relying solely on current OAT. After 2 weeks of learning, algorithm now achieves setpoint within 10 minutes of occupancy start across all weather conditions.

title: Static pressure sensor drift causing VAV starvation on upper floors
description: VAV boxes on floors 9-12 not receiving adequate airflow. Duct static pressure sensor at AHU-6 reading 1.8 in.w.c. but portable manometer shows only 1.1 in.w.c. at the same location. Supply fan running at 78% speed but upper floor zones calling for more air.
resolution: Static pressure sensor diaphragm had developed a pinhole leak causing low reading bias. Replaced sensor and recalibrated against reference gauge. Verified duct static returned to 1.5 in.w.c. setpoint. All VAV boxes on upper floors now receiving design airflow. Added semi-annual sensor calibration to PM schedule.

title: Hot water reset schedule not adjusting based on outdoor air temperature
description: Hot water supply temperature remains at 180°F regardless of outdoor conditions. Reset schedule configured to lower HW temp to 140°F when OAT exceeds 55°F. Building is overheating on mild days and wasting gas.
resolution: OAT sensor wiring had been swapped with return air sensor during a recent panel rewiring. BEMS was reading 72°F return air as outdoor temp, so reset schedule never triggered. Corrected wiring at terminal strip TB-4. Verified HW reset now modulates properly between 140°F and 180°F based on actual OAT.

title: Parking garage CO monitor triggering exhaust fans continuously
description: Underground parking garage exhaust fans running at 100% speed 24/7. CO sensors on level B2 consistently reading 35-50 ppm even during overnight hours when garage is empty. Energy consumption for garage ventilation has tripled.
resolution: CO sensor on level B2 had failed high due to electrolyte depletion (sensor past 5-year life). Replaced both CO sensors on B2 with new electrochemical units. Verified readings dropped to 0-5 ppm overnight. Exhaust fans now modulate between 25% (baseline) and 100% based on actual CO levels. Added sensor replacement schedule to asset management system.

title: Chilled water differential pressure too high causing valve noise
description: Tenants on 3rd floor reporting whistling noise from ceiling. BEMS shows CHW differential pressure at 22 psid, well above the 12 psid setpoint. DP bypass valve appears fully open but pressure remains high. Two-way control valves on floor 3 are throttling hard.
resolution: CHW pump VFD had been placed in manual override at 85% speed by maintenance during a previous event and never returned to auto. Returned VFD to auto control from BEMS DP loop. DP immediately dropped to 12 psid setpoint. Valve noise on floor 3 stopped. Added VFD manual override alarm to BEMS to catch future occurrences.

title: Add occupancy sensor integration for energy savings in open office areas
description: Facilities requesting occupancy-based HVAC and lighting setback for 6 open office areas in Building D. Current system operates on fixed time schedules. Areas are frequently unoccupied during afternoons due to hybrid work policy.
resolution: Installed ceiling-mounted PIR occupancy sensors (one per 400 sq ft zone). Integrated sensors with BEMS via BACnet. Programmed unoccupied setback: HVAC setpoint offset +4°F cooling / -4°F heating, lighting to 30% after 20 minutes of no motion. Implemented a 5-minute grace period before setback activates. Measured 22% reduction in HVAC energy and 35% reduction in lighting energy for the pilot zones.

title: Condenser water treatment chemical feed pump alarm
description: Chemical treatment system for cooling tower condenser water showing pump failure alarm. Conductivity trending upward indicating no chemical dosing. Scale buildup risk if not addressed within 48 hours. Pump motor hums but impeller not turning.
resolution: Chemical feed pump impeller was seized due to crystallized chemical residue from a clogged suction strainer. Disassembled pump, cleaned impeller and housing, replaced suction strainer. Flushed chemical lines and primed pump. Conductivity returned to target range within 6 hours. Added weekly strainer inspection to PM checklist.

title: Discussion on stairwell pressurization fan failure during fire drill
description: During quarterly fire drill, stairwell pressurization fans in Tower B did not activate. Fire command panel sent signal but BEMS showed no fan start command received. Building code requires 0.05 in.w.c. minimum pressure differential. Life safety concern flagged by fire marshal.
resolution: Interposing relay module between fire panel and BEMS fan starter had a blown 24V fuse. Relay was failing silently with no alarm feedback. Replaced fuse and added end-of-line resistor monitoring on the relay circuit to detect future open-circuit faults. Tested all stairwell fans — confirmed proper pressurization at 0.08 in.w.c. Added monthly automated fan test sequence to BEMS schedule.

title: Glycol loop air lock preventing heat transfer in radiant floor system
description: Radiant floor heating in lobby area not warming up despite boiler supplying 140°F water. BEMS shows zone valve open and pump running. Supply and return temperatures are nearly identical (3°F delta vs expected 20°F). Flow meter shows near-zero flow.
resolution: Air lock in the glycol loop at the highest point of the radiant floor circuit (mezzanine level). Opened manual air vent at the high point and bled trapped air for approximately 8 minutes until solid glycol flow was established. Installed automatic air vents at the two highest points in the loop. Delta-T returned to 18°F and lobby temperature reached setpoint within 2 hours.

title: Request for real-time indoor air quality dashboard for tenant wellness program
description: Property management wants a tenant-facing IAQ dashboard displaying CO2, PM2.5, temperature, humidity, and TVOC levels for common areas and major tenant floors. Part of WELL Building certification initiative. Data must update every 5 minutes.
resolution: Deployed 24 multi-sensor IAQ monitors (Airthings) across common areas and tenant floors. Sensors connect via WiFi to cloud platform. Built API integration to pull data into BEMS at 5-minute intervals. Created public-facing dashboard using Grafana with read-only tenant access. Displays real-time values with WELL threshold indicators (green/yellow/red). Historical data retained for 12 months for certification documentation.

title: Kitchen exhaust hood interlock not engaging makeup air unit
description: Commercial kitchen exhaust hood running without makeup air unit (MAU). Kitchen experiencing strong negative pressure pulling unconditioned air through doors. BEMS shows exhaust fan running but MAU in off state. Interlock relay should start MAU when exhaust activates.
resolution: MAU interlock contact was wired to the wrong exhaust fan starter (Fan EF-6 instead of EF-5). When the correct exhaust hood fan started, the interlock was not triggered. Rewired interlock to the correct starter for EF-5. Verified MAU starts within 5 seconds of exhaust fan activation. Kitchen pressure differential now balanced at -0.02 in.w.c. as designed.

title: Troubleshooting intermittent BACnet MSTP token passing errors on trunk 7
description: BACnet MSTP trunk 7 serving the east wing shows frequent token passing errors (10-15% error rate). Controllers randomly drop offline for 30-60 seconds then recover. Issue worsens during high polling periods. Network analyzer shows collisions and retry storms.
resolution: Found two issues: (1) trunk 7 total cable length was 3,800 feet exceeding MSTP maximum of 4,000 feet but with 12 stubs adding effective length. Installed a BACnet router to split trunk into two segments. (2) One controller had a defective RS-485 transceiver pulling the bus low intermittently. Replaced the transceiver chip. Error rate dropped to 0.01% after fixes. Added MSTP trunk health monitoring to BEMS dashboard.

title: AHU-9 return fan tracking not matching supply fan speed
description: AHU-9 return fan running at 30% speed while supply fan is at 65%. Building pressure going highly positive (+0.15 in.w.c.) causing exterior doors difficult to open. Return fan VFD receiving correct speed command from BEMS but actual speed not matching.
resolution: Return fan VFD had a speed reference signal issue — the 0-10V analog output from the controller was only reaching 4.2V maximum due to a failing analog output module. Replaced the DDC analog output module. Return fan now tracks supply fan properly with offset. Building pressure returned to design +0.03 in.w.c.

title: Dual-duct mixing box hot deck valve leaking through
description: Zone 5A on the 7th floor cannot maintain cooling setpoint. BEMS shows cold deck damper fully open and hot deck damper fully closed but discharge temperature is 82°F. Hot deck supply is 120°F. Suspected valve leakage on hot deck.
resolution: Hot deck control valve actuator had mechanically disconnected from the valve stem — the coupler had cracked, so while the actuator showed closed position, the valve was free-floating and gravity was holding it partially open. Replaced actuator coupler and verified valve closure by checking discharge temperature dropped to cold deck supply temp (55°F) when hot deck commanded closed. Zone temperature returned to setpoint.

title: Implement demand response integration with utility grid signal
description: Building owner wants to participate in utility demand response program. Requires BEMS to receive OpenADR signals from the utility and automatically implement load shedding strategies during DR events. Potential revenue of $45K/year from participation.
resolution: Installed OpenADR 2.0b VTN client on BEMS server. Configured three DR shed levels: Level 1 (global setpoint adjust +2°F), Level 2 (dim non-essential lighting 30%, raise setpoint +4°F), Level 3 (shed non-critical loads, max setpoint offset +6°F, reduce ventilation to ASHRAE minimums). Tested each level during a simulated DR event. Peak demand reduced by 280kW at Level 3. Set up auto-notification to facility manager when DR events are dispatched.

title: Investigating mysterious after-hours energy spikes on weekends
description: Energy dashboard showing unexplained 150kW spikes between 2:00 AM and 4:00 AM on Saturday and Sunday mornings. No scheduled operations during those times. Spikes last approximately 45 minutes. Facility manager suspects unauthorized equipment usage.
resolution: Traced spikes to the domestic hot water recirculation system. Timer had been programmed to run the DHW recirc pumps and electric booster heater on a 24/7 schedule instead of the intended weekday-only schedule. The 2 AM spike coincided with the system's high-demand recovery cycle heating the entire storage tank. Corrected DHW schedule to match building occupancy. Weekend energy baseline dropped by 140kW during those hours.

title: Emergency generator auto-transfer switch not communicating with BEMS
description: BEMS lost all monitoring points for the emergency generator and automatic transfer switch (ATS) two weeks ago. No alarms, fuel level, run status, or transfer position data available. Generator PM is overdue and fuel level is unknown. ATS is Cummins OTEC with Modbus interface.
resolution: Modbus RS-485 communication cable between ATS and BEMS had been accidentally disconnected during UPS battery replacement work in the electrical room. Cable was lying loose behind the UPS rack. Reconnected cable to BEMS Modbus gateway port 3. Verified all 28 monitoring points came back online. Fuel level was at 62% — scheduled delivery. Added cable labels and conduit protection for critical communication runs.

title: Perimeter baseboard heaters activating in summer
description: South-facing perimeter zones in Building C activating baseboard heaters despite outdoor temperature of 88°F. Occupants complaining of excessive heat near windows. BEMS shows baseboard heating valve open at 40%. Zone thermostat calling for cooling, not heating.
resolution: Zone controller sequence of operations had a logic error in the deadband calculation. When cooling setpoint (74°F) minus deadband (6°F) yielded 68°F, and the zone temp briefly dipped to 68°F due to overcooling from the VAV, the baseboard heating loop activated. Reduced deadband from 6°F to 3°F and added an outdoor air temperature lockout (disable baseboards when OAT > 65°F). Issue resolved across all 14 perimeter zones using the same template.

title: Coordinating BEMS upgrade from legacy Niagara N4 to current version
description: Team planning discussion on upgrading Building A BEMS from Niagara Framework N4.6 to N4.13. System has 4,200 points across 38 JACE controllers. Concerned about driver compatibility, schedule preservation, and graphic migration. Upgrade window is the holiday shutdown period.
resolution: Developed phased upgrade plan: (1) Back up all JACE station databases and graphics. (2) Upgrade supervisor workstation first and verify driver compatibility matrix. (3) Upgrade JACEs in groups of 5 during off-hours with rollback capability. (4) Found 3 legacy Lon drivers needed updated versions — obtained from Tridium partner. (5) Graphics required minor CSS adjustments for new HTML5 rendering engine. Full upgrade completed in 4 days during holiday week. All 4,200 points verified operational. New features: improved trending, enhanced cybersecurity modules, and mobile-responsive graphics.

title: Humidifier generating mineral dust deposits in ductwork
description: White mineral dust accumulating on diffuser grilles and furniture in zones served by AHU-3. AHU-3 has an ultrasonic humidifier using city water supply. Water hardness is 220 ppm. Dust is calcium carbonate residue from water mineralization.
resolution: Ultrasonic humidifiers aerosolize minerals in tap water, depositing white dust downstream. Replaced ultrasonic humidifier with an evaporative steam humidifier that produces pure steam and leaves minerals behind in the cylinder. Connected humidifier drain to condensate line. White dust issue completely eliminated. Cleaned downstream ductwork and diffusers. Added water softener upstream of humidifier as supplemental protection.

title: Rooftop unit compressor short cycling on low suction pressure
description: RTU-4 compressor cycling every 4-5 minutes on low suction pressure cutout. BEMS shows suction pressure dropping to 45 psig (cutout is 50 psig for R-410A). Evaporator coil appears to be frosting despite airflow being normal. Superheat is running at 25°F (target 10-12°F).
resolution: Thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) sensing bulb had lost its charge due to a micro-crack in the capillary tube. TXV was not opening sufficiently, starving the evaporator of refrigerant and causing low suction pressure and high superheat. Replaced TXV assembly including sensing bulb and capillary. After replacement: suction pressure stable at 118 psig, superheat at 11°F, no more short cycling.

title: Configure automated fault detection and diagnostics for central plant
description: Engineering team requesting AFDD rules for the central chiller/boiler plant to proactively identify equipment degradation, inefficiencies, and impending failures. Want automated daily reports and real-time critical alerts. Current approach is reactive — issues only found when tenants complain.
resolution: Implemented 35 AFDD rules covering: chiller COP degradation (>15% from baseline), condenser approach temperature rise, evaporator fouling index, pump differential pressure anomalies, VFD fault frequency tracking, simultaneous heating and cooling detection, HW/CHW reset effectiveness, stuck valve detection (command vs position mismatch >5min), and sensor drift correlation. Rules run every 15 minutes against live data. Daily summary email to plant engineer. Critical faults (potential equipment damage) trigger immediate SMS alert. Dashboard shows fault history and trending. Identified 3 latent issues in first week of operation.

title: Investigating thermal comfort complaints in open plan office despite BEMS showing setpoint met
description: Repeated thermal comfort complaints from east wing open plan office. BEMS shows zone temperature at 72°F setpoint. However, occupants near windows report feeling cold in winter and hot in summer. Perimeter vs interior temperature differential suspected. Single zone sensor located in interior ceiling plenum.
resolution: Installed 4 supplementary wireless temperature sensors at desk level (3 feet) in the complaint zones — 2 perimeter, 2 interior. Data showed perimeter temps were 66°F in winter and 78°F in summer while the interior ceiling sensor read 72°F. Repositioned the primary zone sensor to a representative location between perimeter and interior at desk height. Added a second perimeter zone with independent VAV control. Installed low-E solar film on east-facing windows to reduce radiant heat gain/loss. Complaints dropped to zero after modifications.

title: Elevator lobby pressurization fan noise complaint at night
description: Security guards reporting loud fan noise from elevator lobbies on floors 6-10 between midnight and 6 AM. BEMS shows elevator lobby pressurization fans running at 100% speed continuously. Building is in unoccupied mode. Fans should modulate based on stack effect pressure.
resolution: Pressurization fan control loop was referencing a DP sensor that had been removed during a renovation 3 months ago. With no sensor feedback, the PI loop was winding up to maximum output. Installed new differential pressure sensor across the elevator lobby door frame. Recalibrated PI loop for 0.03 in.w.c. setpoint. Fans now modulate between 20-60% depending on stack effect conditions. Noise complaints resolved. Added sensor health monitoring alarm to detect future sensor failures.

title: Condensate drain pan overflow flooding ceiling tiles below AHU-7
description: Water-stained ceiling tiles discovered below AHU-7 mechanical room. Condensate drain pan overflowing during high humidity days. BEMS shows no condensate pan high-level alarm despite water visibly overflowing. Drain line appears connected and not visibly blocked at the unit.
resolution: Condensate drain line had developed an algae plug approximately 15 feet downstream inside the wall chase. Water backed up and overflowed the primary pan. Secondary (emergency) drain pan float switch was stuck in the down position due to mineral deposits — which is why no alarm was generated. Cleared drain line with compressed nitrogen, treated with algaecide tablets. Cleaned and freed secondary pan float switch. Added condensate pan water detection sensor wired directly to BEMS (bypassing the unreliable float switch). Installed clear P-trap for visual inspection.

title: Implement nighttime building flush sequence for improved morning IAQ
description: Green building consultant recommending a pre-occupancy flush cycle to purge stale air and VOCs that accumulate overnight. Building has tight envelope with low infiltration. Morning CO2 readings are 800-900 ppm at occupancy start. Target is below 600 ppm when occupants arrive.
resolution: Programmed a 90-minute pre-occupancy flush sequence starting 1.5 hours before scheduled occupancy. AHUs operate at 100% outdoor air with maximum fan speed during flush. Added OAT lockout — flush disabled when OAT is below 32°F or above 90°F to prevent energy waste and freeze risk. Economizer dampers go to maximum OA position during flush, then return to normal DCV control at occupancy. CO2 readings at occupancy start now average 450 ppm. Estimated IAQ improvement supports LEED IEQ credits. Energy impact is minimal due to mild early morning temperatures during most of the year.
